cd /tmp/probe-api/final-race && for i in $(seq 16); do BUN_DEBUG_QUIET_LOGS=1 NO_COLOR=1 timeout 120 /workspace/bun/build/debug/bun-debug build ./entry.js --minify-syntax --target=node --outfile=out.mjs 2>&1 | grep -c '^error:'; done
(fold off: the same with BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_DISABLE_CONST_CALL_FOLDING=1)
API form: run `bun-debug build.mjs` 8 times.
defects.fold_on:
Number of errors in 16 runs: 2 1 1 2 2 1 1 2 1 2 2 2 1 2 1 1 (exit code 1 each time).
A run with 1 error prints only `error: Could not resolve: "./missing.js"`. A run with 2 errors also prints `error: Unexpected }` for node_modules/flags/package.json.
API, 8 runs: logs: 2, 2, 1, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1. The order of the two messages also changes.
defects.fold_off:
Number of errors in 16 runs: 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2.
API, 8 runs: logs: 2 each time, same order.
defects.suspected_cause: Same cause as the defect above, plus a race. The resolver reports the package.json error one time per process, to the log of the worker whose lookup reads the directory first. When that worker parses a.js (which has an import that does not resolve) the log of its parse task is dropped, when it parses b.js the error is kept. The ratio depends on timing: without the `pad` line in a.js I got 1 run of 10 with 2 errors, with 40 such lines all runs had 2 errors.

defects.suspected_cause: Against the rule that a resolver message of the lookup is in the build log one time. The resolver logs this error on each call (src/resolver/resolver.rs about line 5816, in the path that loads a file: an `EntriesOption::Err` entry is logged each time it is read), not one time per directory like a package.json error. The resolve succeeds through the second `paths` entry, so the log of the parse task is kept, and the error is logged by the lookup and again by the bundle thread. An unreadable node_modules directory (/tmp/probe-api/perm2) gives one error both ways, because that path caches the failure.

defects.title: Docs say a call of an import from a package with both "main" and "module" is not replaced. With --target=node it is replaced
defects.command: cd /tmp/probe-api/docs-dual && for target in node browser bun; do BUN_DEBUG_QUIET_LOGS=1 NO_COLOR=1 timeout 120 /workspace/bun/build/debug/bun-debug build ./entry.js --minify-syntax --target=$target --outfile=out-$target.mjs; cat out-$target.mjs; done
defects.fold_off: The call is kept for each target. What the bundles print is the same both ways (`off`), so this is a difference with the docs only, not a wrong output.
defects.suspected_cause: The lookup skips a package only when the resolver gives a second path (`has_second_build` in src/bundler/const_call_lookup.rs). For the node target the resolver takes "main" and gives no second path, so the fold is safe there. The sentence in docs/bundler/index.mdx ("The bundler does not replace a call of an import from a package that has both a \"main\" and a \"module\" file") has no such condition. This is a fold that the docs say does not happen, not a missed fold. The other import rules of the docs section held in /tmp/probe-api/docs (export default, export *, CommonJS export, const arrow, ns.isDev(), import attribute, redirect file, wrapper of one level, chain of 8 files, literal arguments, no fold without a condition).

api.held_up:
All of this showed no difference between fold on and fold off (same `success`, same `logs`, same output of the bundle). Cases are under /tmp/probe-api/cases/, the harness is /tmp/probe-api/lib.mjs and run.sh.

In-memory `files`:
- a file that shadows the file on disk, a file that is only in memory, an in-memory entry point, all files in memory
- keys `./env.js`, `env.js`, and keys that are not normalized
- values as string, Uint8Array, ArrayBuffer, Blob, with a byte order mark, empty, with a syntax error, CommonJS, without the export
- names that are not ASCII
- in-memory files later in a chain (re-export, redirect file, wrapper)

Plugins:
- onLoad: filter matches or does not match the imported file, sync and async, returns undefined, namespace `file`, another namespace, flag `i`, filter on the absolute directory, filter on the importer only
- onResolve: match, no match, async, returns undefined, `external: true`, to a virtual namespace
- a virtual module as the importer, with relative and absolute imports
- a plugin that matches a file later in a chain (13 variants)
- `defer()` on the imported file, on the importer, on another file
- async `setup()`, two plugins, a plugin that changes `build.config`, a filter added in `onStart` (also with a delay), a filter added too late
- plugin errors (throw, reject, bad contents) with `throw: false` and `throw: true`: the only difference is the intended one (import in a dead branch)
- plugins that match every path and record what the bundler resolves and loads: same list both ways for `require(name)`, `require.resolve`, `import()`, templates, `new URL`
- a macro runs the same number of times both ways

Two builds in one process:
- other `define`, `files`, `conditions`, `features`, `tsconfig`, `target`, with and without plugins, one after the other and at the same time: no value of one build is in another build
- the file on disk changes between builds, files are added to or removed from the directory between builds
- 120 importers and 40 packages, 4 builds at the same time, 3 rounds: same output, no crash, no ASAN report
- `BUN_DEBUG_const_call=1`: each imported file is parsed at most 2 times per build (depth 0 and depth 1), also with 3 builds at the same time
- the bundle text with fold on is the same in 3 runs

Options:
- `external` (exact, `*`, glob, absolute), `packages: "external"`, external package by name: an external import is never folded
- `target` browser, node, bun with the `browser` field and `exports` conditions; a package on disk with the name of a module that Bun replaces (`node-fetch`, `ws`) is not folded for target bun and its package.json is not read
- HTML entry point, server file that imports an HTML file (two targets in one build)
- `format` esm, cjs, iife; `minify: true`, identifiers, whitespace with keepNames; `splitting` with shared and lazy chunks; `naming`; `banner` and `footer`; `sourcemap` inline and linked (same mapped positions); `compile`; `bytecode`; `drop`; `env` inline, prefix, disable; `loader`; `reactFastRefresh`, `reactCompiler`
- `imports` field, directory import, symbolic link, package that names itself, `browser` field that maps or turns off a relative file
- side effects of the imported file stay, in the same order, also when the importer becomes empty and in .ts importers with other unused names in the same import
- self import, re-export cycle, redirect cycle, wrapper cycle, 5000 character specifier, 200000 nested brackets in the imported file: no hang, no crash
- resolver warnings and errors in a build where all imports resolve: same both ways, one time
